titleEn: One Hand for Baby, One for Mio!

pages.text: "Mom, look at this!" Mio, who wanted to do everything alone, waved a paper butterfly. Grown-ups stood by the yard gate. Time to go home. But Mom was holding and patting the baby.
"Shh, the baby is sleeping. A little quieter," Mom whispered. Mio pouted. "Then I will go alone!" Mio turned away and gripped both bag straps.
Mio strode ahead without looking back. Mom's footsteps grew farther away. The paper butterfly fluttered only in Mio's hand.
Mio stood alone by the gate. Other children left one by one, holding grown-ups' hands. There was nobody to show the butterfly to.
Mio put the butterfly back in the bag. Their nose tingled. "Going alone... is no fun at all."
Mom reached the gate. "Mio, let us go together." Still turned away, Mio said softly, "I can go alone."
Mio glanced back. Mom held the baby in one arm; her other hand was empty. She waved it and sang, "One hand for baby, one for Mio!"
Teacher Bau knelt in front of Mio. "Mio, whose place is that empty hand?" Mio said very softly, "...Mine."
Mio ran over and held Mom's hand. "One, baby in Mom's arm! Two, the empty hand is for mine! Three, side by side through the gate!" Mio took out the butterfly and fluttered it before Mom's nose.
Mom hugged Mio. "What a lovely butterfly." Even with a baby, one of Mom's hands was always Mio's place. Mio gripped it tightly and called, "One hand for baby, one for Mio!"
